## Observation

A `make verify` on arm64 macOS (2026-10-27) failed 22 tests plus 1 error, all in 4 files that drive `infra/scripts/observability.sh` (`test_observability_mcp_health_9ea3.py`, `_offsets_6a65.py`, `_marker_anchor_8c2f.py`, `_mcp_markers.py`). Each failing case raised `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` after the tests' 60 s bound; stderr also named `/var/lib/rebar/probe-region` and `/var/lib/rebar/reviewbot-webhook-auth-offset` as missing. Reproduction evidence is in the comments.

## Root cause

1. **The tests reach the host's real Docker daemon with no bound.** The script calls `docker system df`, `docker ps` and `docker stats --no-stream` through `clamped`/`bounded`. On a host without coreutils `timeout` (stock macOS), `bounded` deliberately runs the command unbounded. 12 of the 19 test files that run the whole script do not stub `docker`, so each run waits on the host daemon: measured 6 s (`system df`) + 3 s (`stats`) per run on colima, 16–17 s per script run versus 5 s with `docker` stubbed. Under load this exceeds 60 s; a `docker` stub that stalls reproduces the exact `TimeoutExpired` signature.
2. **Timeouts orphan the script.** `subprocess.run(..., timeout=...)` kills only the direct `bash`; the script's subshells and their children survive at PPID 1 (16 orphaned pairs measured after the 2026-10-27 run; reproduced here).
3. **No test redirects every host state path.** The script defaults 17 state paths (lines 33, 34, 67, 77, 920, 952, 971, 992, 1013–1018, 1021, 1022, 1076) to `/var/lib/rebar/...` (`NAME="${NAME:-/var/lib/rebar/...}"`). Every one of the 19 files leaves between 4 and 15 of the 17 unset, so runs try to read and write the real host directory. On this host the writes fail silently (`2>/dev/null || true`), so this is not what times out — but a host where `/var/lib/rebar` exists (the production layout) would have test runs read and overwrite real offset state, and nothing stops a new path being added unredirected.

The missing-path stderr lines are a symptom, not the cause of the timeout: the script continues and exits 0.

## Approach (test-side; production defaults unchanged)

Scope: all 19 files under `tests/scripts/test_observability_*.py` that run the whole script. The other 2 (`_cap_deps`, `_pct_of_cap_b380`) only read the script text or run one extracted function, and are left as they are.

1. Add one shared helper module `tests/_observability_harness.py` (beside `tests/_subprocess_env.py`, so a nested pytest that loads a test module as a plugin can import it; `test_observability_exit.py` gets the same explicit `tests/` sys.path bootstrap `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` uses for that case). It passes the redacted `SubprocessEnv` through without unwrapping it:
   - `state_path_defaults()` parses the script for every `NAME="${NAME:-/var/lib/rebar/...}"` default (17 today; the number is derived from the script, never hard-coded), so a path added to the script is redirected without editing any test.
   - `INSTANCE_ID_CACHE` (line 73) has no literal default: it derives from the directory of `REGION_CACHE`, so redirecting `REGION_CACHE` redirects it. The helper also sets it explicitly to the same `tmp_path` directory so the redirect does not depend on that derivation.
   - `observability_env(tmp_path)` returns the subprocess environment with every such variable pointing into `tmp_path`, and a fallback `docker` stub (`exit 1`, i.e. unavailable) placed ahead of the host `PATH`. A test's own `bin/` stubs are prepended after it, so tests that stub `docker` keep their stub. Test-specific overrides still win because tests update the env afterwards.
   - `run_observability(argv, env=..., timeout=...)` starts the script in its own session and, on timeout, kills the whole process group and reaps it before re-raising `TimeoutExpired`. Before starting, it refuses (AssertionError naming the variable and its default) any env in which a state variable still resolves under `/var/lib/rebar`, or whose `docker` is the host's binary, so an unredirected path fails fast in under a second instead of timing out.
2. Convert the 19 files to build their env with `observability_env` and run the script with `run_observability`. No assertion, stub or scenario changes; existing per-file timeouts (60/120/180/300 s) are kept.
3. Add the guard test `tests/scripts/test_observability_harness_isolation.py`:
   - every non-comment `/var/lib/rebar` literal in the script sits in a parsed `${NAME:-...}` default (a hard-coded path fails and names its line);
   - the number of parsed defaults equals the number of non-comment lines naming `/var/lib/rebar`, and includes the 17 names present today (anti-vacuity for the parser);
   - `INSTANCE_ID_CACHE` is set under `tmp_path` by `observability_env`, and the script still derives it from `REGION_CACHE`'s directory (if that derivation changes, the test names it);
   - no test file in `tests/scripts/` runs `observability.sh` (or a copy) through `subprocess` directly — every whole-script run goes through `run_observability` (AST scan; names file and line);
   - `run_observability` rejects an env missing one state variable, naming it;
   - an induced timeout (stub that sleeps) leaves no surviving `observability.sh` process.
4. Do not change `infra/scripts/observability.sh`, raise the 60 s bound, skip, or mark any test platform-specific.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every one of the script's `/var/lib/rebar` defaults (17 today) is set under `tmp_path` by `observability_env`, verified by `test_observability_env_redirects_every_state_path`.
- [x] `run_observability` refuses an env that leaves any state variable under `/var/lib/rebar`, naming the variable, in under 5 s; verified by a guard test that deletes `REGION_CACHE`.
- [x] A non-comment `/var/lib/rebar` literal outside a `NAME="${NAME:-...}"` default fails the guard test, which names its line.
- [x] No test in `tests/scripts/` runs `observability.sh` (or a copy) through `subprocess` directly; the AST guard names any file and line that does, and its anti-vacuity case proves it detects one.
- [x] `run_observability` refuses, naming the path, an env whose `PATH` resolves `docker` to the same binary the ambient `PATH` resolves; a guard test proves the refusal, so every whole-script run uses the fallback stub or the test's own.
- [x] After an induced timeout, the stalled probe's grandchild process is gone within 10 s.
- [x] `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_*.py` passes on arm64 macOS with no manual host setup.
- [x] `/var/lib/rebar` does not exist on this host after that run.
- [x] `pytest tests/scripts/` passes.
- [x] `make lint` exits 0.
- [x] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [x] `git diff origin/main -- infra/scripts/observability.sh` is empty.
- [x] No test is skipped or marked platform-specific by this change.
- [x] Per-run script time with real docker versus the stub is recorded on this ticket, before and after the change.

Not in scope: bug `degraded-chilly-galago` (pandoc on arm64), which is the other blocker for a green `make verify` on arm64 macOS.
